cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. Production systems of comparable complexity typically maintain 40 to 60% coverage. This gap means regressions can reach production unchallenged, creating risk that grows with each deployment.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH, with no defined rollback procedure in place. The last rollback attempt, eight months ago, required over three hours to complete and revealed no documented path for reverting a failed release. This creates a critical dependency on one person and leaves the system exposed to prolonged outages if a deployment fails and reversal is needed.

evidence_before_interpretation.detail: first sentence contains no concrete figure, expected one for this case's facts: 'Deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH, with no defined rollback procedure in place.'

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented handover process, and that engineer works on a rolling month-to-month contract. A departure would leave the company unable to access its own database until credentials could be rotated—a process that typically requires downtime and may take days if undocumented. There is no compensating control: no shared credential store, no backup access path, and no procedure to execute in this scenario. This is a critical exposure of availability.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely, with no documented deletion policy and no process for handling data-subject deletion requests. This creates direct exposure under GDPR and similar regimes, where deletion rights are mandatory and enforced through substantial fines. The company has no compensating control: retention decisions rest entirely on individual discretion, and no audit trail documents what data exists or when it was collected. We recommend establishing a data retention schedule, documenting deletion procedures, and implementing technical controls to enforce both.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage stands at 31%, with no automated gate in continuous integration to block deployments below a threshold. Three of the last four production incidents originated in untested edge cases that coverage would have caught. Deployments are manual, and there is no documented rollback procedure, so a defect that reaches production cannot be rapidly contained. The combination means a regression can move to customers without technical challenge, detection, or reversal.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. This means any database access exposes all user credentials to whoever holds the access, including support staff, backup systems, and any attacker who breaches the database layer. No hashing or salting is in place. Plaintext storage is incompatible with any security posture, and must be treated as live customer data exposure.

Deployments are carried out manually with no documented or automated rollback procedure. When a deployment fails or introduces a regression, the path back to a working state requires manual intervention and institutional knowledge of the system. No staging environment exists to test the deployment process itself. The absence of a rollback path means each production release carries unquantified risk.

Code comments follow inconsistent style across the codebase, with no linting rule or architectural decision enforcing a convention. Inconsistency makes skimming for relevant context harder and signals lack of ownership across teams. No linting gate blocks a merge, so new comments follow whatever pattern was present locally. Standardizing on a single style and enforcing it in CI would surface comments earlier and reduce cognitive load in code review.
